text:
The swing shortfall is the only failing spec, and its two limits point to the cascode bias devices. The upper limit (swing_hi = 1.297 V) is set by the PMOS cascode gate voltage pc, and that voltage comes entirely from the diode-connected Mb4. Mb4 is much narrower than the mirror ratio suggests, so its Vsg is large and pc sits low. Mb5 is the analogous NMOS bias for nc, which sets the lower limit (swing_lo = 0.33 V), so it is the second suspect. This is a judgment from the netlist and measured swings, not a simulation, so the ranking is tentative.

```json
{"ranking": ["Mb4", "Mb5", "M6"], "fault": "Mb4 (PMOS diode generating the cascode gate bias pc) is undersized at W=0.4607 um. Its large Vsg pulls pc low, which caps the upper output swing (vout_max ~ pc + |Vtp|). Restoring a proper width for the pc bias should recover the roughly 0.11 V swing deficit."}
```
